Task:
Look into GitHub issue 40 on TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin: "Elegoo Centauri Carbon (Elegoo Link): cannot connect from the chat to send prints". The reporter added a Centauri Carbon in JusPrin 2.0.0, but the printer chat only connects Moonraker and OctoPrint printers, so it never tried to connect. They also asked whether OctoEverywhere works.

Find out how the printer connect flow decides which connection types it offers (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/ and the per-connection-type connection skills), and what OrcaSlicer upstream already supports for Elegoo Link / Centauri Carbon (check upstream's print host types before building anything). Reproduce the reporter's experience in the real app first: add a Centauri Carbon and ask the chat to connect it.

Done means one of these: connecting a Centauri Carbon from the chat works and is tested (unit tests plus a real-app or simulator check), or, if that is not feasible now, a short written finding explaining what support exists, what is missing, and what it would take, so Kenneth can decide. Do not post on the GitHub issue, commit to jusprin-dev, or push without Kenneth's approval.

---
name: connect-print-host
trigger: connect_print_host
---

# Connecting a printer through Moonraker or OctoPrint

The rules above still apply. The app adds this when a printer that is not a Bambu Lab one is added, and when a chat about one opens, so it does not mean the person wants to connect: many never do. Start connecting only once they say they want to. Right after a printer is added, unless they have already said whether they want it connected, offer it once: end that reply with exactly "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" and then "Choices: Connect it | Not now". When they have already asked to connect it, go straight on.

Once they want to connect, your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention. Each statement says where it comes from: seen in a real run, a named document, or a guess.

## Moonraker or OctoPrint

The app connects to one of two programs that run beside the printer, and printer_host_connect needs to know which:

- **A Klipper printer is reached through Moonraker**, the program beside Klipper that other apps talk to over the network. People usually use it through a web page in a browser, Mainsail or Fluidd. The app talks only to Moonraker.
- **OctoPrint runs on a computer beside the printer and drives it.** People use it through OctoPrint's own web page. The app talks only to OctoPrint, never to the printer itself.

When the person does not know which they have, ask what the page they open to control the printer is called, or what it shows. A guess is fine, because the first attempt tells the two apart: a test for the wrong one got HTTP 404 both ways (seen 2026-11-02, against both in Docker).

## The address

Ask for the address they open that page at, including any port.

- **Moonraker:** the app needs Moonraker's own address, port 7125 unless it was changed, as in `http://192.168.1.50:7125`. The address of the Mainsail page answered too where that page passed the app's requests on to Moonraker, as a usual Mainsail setup does. A Mainsail page that did not pass them on answered with a web page instead (both seen 2026-11-02 in Docker). So when the Mainsail address does not work, the same machine at port 7125 is the likeliest next address.
- **OctoPrint:** the address they open OctoPrint at.
- The address can be an IP address or a name, but a name this computer cannot look up got no answer at all (seen 2026-11-02 with a `.local` name no device answered to).
- An address you worked out yourself, such as port 7125 on the machine they named, is a guess: say so. When they say to try it, call printer_host_connect with it at once, without asking again.

## The key

printer_host_connect tests the address during the call, for up to 30 seconds, with the key the app already holds for that address or with none. A first try without a key is fine: the answer says whether one is needed. When the host asks for a key, the call stays open and shows the app's key form in the chat. Never ask for the key in chat. The form has three ways out: Connect, which tests again with what they typed; "Help me find the key"; and Cancel. Each ends the call, so its result is the outcome, whichever way it went. When they asked for help finding the key, or closed the form, nothing more was sent, and the result still gives the host's first refusal.

**Moonraker.** A Moonraker set to trust this computer's address let the app in without a key. One that did not answered HTTP 401 Unauthorized, the same answer for no key and for a wrong key (seen 2026-11-02 in Docker), so the result says which key each test sent: none, the one typed in the form, or the one saved for this printer. Most people at home have no key and do not know what one is, so after a 401 do not ask them to type one. What helps them:

- **The likeliest fix on a home network needs no key.** Moonraker lets in only the addresses in `trusted_clients`, under `[authorization]` in `moonraker.conf`, its settings file on the printer's computer. Mainsail's own FAQ for its "connection unauthorized" error says to add the network there, written like `192.168.1.0/24` for the addresses 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.254, and then restart Moonraker. That this is their cause is a guess. Where they can edit that file depends on their setup, so search for their version before you say.
- **A key, if they want one.** Moonraker's installation documentation gives the key page as `http://{moonraker-host}/access/api_key`, with no port. The page is Moonraker's own, so it is at Moonraker's address and port, the one that answered 401, as in `http://192.168.1.50:7125/access/api_key`. A page not reached at another port says nothing about the key. The same documentation says to open the page from a trusted client, so a computer Moonraker does not trust may be refused there too. Over SSH on the printer's computer, it gives the script `~/moonraker/scripts/fetch-apikey.sh`.
- Mainsail's FAQ for this error points to `trusted_clients`, not to a key, and no Mainsail or Fluidd page that shows the key was found in their documentation (searched 2026-11-04). Do not send the person looking for one.

**OctoPrint.** It needs a key. Without one, the OctoPrint tried (1.9.3, in Docker, 2026-11-02) answered only to refuse, HTTP 403 "You don't have the permission to access the requested resource". A wrong key got HTTP 403 "Invalid API key", so the two can be told apart. OctoPrint's API documentation says a user's own key is shown in their user settings, and in the user list of its Access Control settings, and the global key in its API settings. Versions differ, so search for where theirs shows it before you say, and ask what they see.

## When it is verified

The result is `verified`, and the app has saved the address as this printer's connection.

- **Moonraker:** the app asked Moonraker for its server information. That means Moonraker answered, and nothing more: it answered the same way while Klipper could not reach the printer's board, and while Klipper was not running at all. What says whether the printer can print is Klipper's state, which the result gives after "Moonraker reports Klipper's state as". Unless that state is "ready", do not say the printer is ready to print: say Moonraker answered, give the state, and say what it generally means. Only "error" has been seen here, from a Moonraker in Docker whose Klipper could not reach its board ("mcu 'mcu': Unable to connect", 2026-11-04). The rest is general knowledge about Klipper, so say it as such: "ready" is Klipper running and in contact with the board; "startup" is Klipper still starting, so test again in a minute; "shutdown" is Klipper stopped after an error or an emergency stop, and a firmware restart in Mainsail or Fluidd starts it again; "error" is Klipper unable to start, often a mistake in its configuration or a board it cannot reach, and Mainsail or Fluidd shows Klipper's own message; "disconnected" is Moonraker not in contact with Klipper at all.
- **OctoPrint:** the app asked OctoPrint for its version. That means OctoPrint answered and took the key, and nothing more: it answered the same way with no printer attached to it.

## What the tools report

- `not_configured` means no connection has been saved yet. `unknown` means one is saved and has not been tested in this chat.
- `verified` means the host accepted the test and the app saved the address.
- `failed` comes with what the app's test was told, in the host's own words where it gave any.

## When a connection fails

Say what the app saw in the person's terms, then work out why. What the test was told says which step to suspect. Each of these was seen on 2026-11-02 through the app's own test, against Moonraker, Mainsail and OctoPrint in Docker:

- **HTTP 401 Unauthorized.** Moonraker answered and did not let the app in. The address is right; see the key above.
- **HTTP 403 "You don't have the permission…" or "Invalid API key".** OctoPrint answered and got no key, or refused the one it got. The address is right.
- **HTTP 404.** Something answered at that address, but not as the chosen program answers. This came when OctoPrint was chosen for a Moonraker, and when Moonraker was chosen for an OctoPrint, so the other one at the same address is the next try.
- **"Could not parse Moonraker server response".** A web server answered with a page. This came from a Mainsail page that did not pass requests on. Moonraker's port, 7125, on the same machine is worth trying.
- **"Connection refused".** The machine at that address answered at once, but nothing was listening on that port. The port may be wrong, or the program may not be running.
- **"Connection timed out", after about 10 seconds.** Nothing answered. This came from an address with no device on it, and also from `https://` in front of a server that speaks plain `http://`, so despite what the message says about the network, an `https://` address is worth trying with `http://` first.
- **No answer after 30 seconds.** The test was still waiting. This came from a name ending in `.local` that no device answered to. The IP address, which their router or Mainsail may show, avoids looking up the name.

What is worth trying beyond this has not been tested here, so search for what people with the same setup report before you suggest it. Without a search, general knowledge gives: opening the same address in a browser on this computer, checking the printer's computer and this one are on the same network, or restarting the program. When they want to try again, call printer_host_connect again with the address to use.

## When they are stuck

The JusPrin developers can only fix what they hear about, and they have not tested most setups. A person who has tried and wants them to know can report it with `issue_report_open`, which opens a GitHub issue page in their browser with your summary filled in. It files nothing: they read the page, change it if they like, and submit it with their own GitHub account.

Kenneth settled this on 2026-09-23. In the printer setup flow, "connect your printer" is user wording. For the code it means: find or enter the printer's connection details, check that they work, and save them with that printer. The check may open a real connection for a moment. On jusprin-newui, 264d6f8141 removes the override and bd8ea51abc adds the harness checks. With it gone, selecting a non-Bambu profile gives the connection software back to Orca's profile-driven choice, the same as stock Orca.

**How to apply:**
- Don't add code that keeps a printer connection alive across profile changes unless Kenneth asks for that behavior explicitly.
- After the connection software changes, printer status stays "connected" for up to 30 seconds. That is the normal freshness window in `has_recent_printer_data`, the same one that applies when a printer is switched off. It is not a regression.

**Recipe.** Start `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --manual-mcp <scratch dir>` with `HOME=<scratch home>`, wait for `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY` on stderr (about 15 s), read the URL from `<scratch dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`, then call tools with `probe.call(urlsplit(url), "tools/call", {"name": ..., "arguments": ...})` imported from `tests/mcp/probe.py`. Another session's harness can run at the same time; the port falls back from 47301 and the discovery file is per data dir.

**Trap 1: leaked harness.** In a script, `cd "$S" && nohup harness ... &` makes `$!` the subshell, so `kill $!` leaves the harness running, and the next run's `rm -rf <fixture>` fails with "Directory not empty". Write `cd "$S"; nohup harness ... &`. Check with `pgrep -fl "<worktree>.*JusPrinShellHarness"` before finishing.

**Trap 2: slice_start on a sliced, unchanged plate.** The fixture's plate 1 starts sliced. `slice_start` on it (with or without `wait`) left it reported `sliced: false`, `slice_report` `valid: false`, and with `wait: true` the probe saw the stream close with no reply. Orca's log says "background process in idle state, use previous result". Change a setting first, then slice. Not investigated further.

**Timings on this Mac, Release config, load 30 to 40:** fresh worktree build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests workspace_contract_tests setting_display_tests shell_integration_harness` was 905 steps in about 14 min; the shell harness default regression (549 checks) about 2 min; the workspace adapter harness (972 checks) under 1 min. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

**Seeding a preset (2026-10-12).** `--manual-mcp` does not wipe its directory at start, so a user preset written to `<fixture>/user/default/machine/<name>.json` before launch (keys `from: User`, `inherits`, `name`, `printer_settings_id`, `version`, plus the values under test) is loaded and can be named as a settings `target.preset`. A Python driver that starts the harness with `subprocess.Popen` and terminates it in `finally` avoids Trap 1.


**Why a plate will not slice (2026-10-15).** MCP `slice_report` on a plate Orca refuses says only `valid: false`, with no reason even with `sections: ["findings"]`, and `slice_start` still answers `started: true`. Orca's own refusal text is in `<fixture>/log/debug_*.log`: grep `validate err=`. Used to reproduce the PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate case (branch `claude/bed-type-mismatch`, worktree distracted-lehmann-9c1b12). See [[printer-setup-bed-type-check]].

- Kill the app before editing the conf. Replace a scratch binary with `rm` then `cp`: `cp` over a binary that has run gets the new process killed at launch.
- `Contents/Resources` in the build is a symlink to the worktree. Replace it with a real folder of links before corrupting a resource, or the worktree gets corrupted.
- Bringing the app forward triggers an account refresh, so to race the gateway (a real 402), change the ledger and send without refocusing.
- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.
- A compose recreate drops env set by a wrapper; check `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` before any chat so only the fake upstream is reachable.

Still needs the screen: pointer hover, native file dialogs, Orca's wizard.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

Two things about `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py` as of b7ac9b4c90:

- It records no token use. To report it, wrap `suite.post` from a scratch script and log each response's `usage`, leaving the runner unchanged. OpenRouter's `usage` has a `cost` field; OpenAI's does not.

The search turned up protocol details for the Centauri Carbon's port 3030 interface, but no mature, dedicated simulator.

- **Endpoint:** The printer's URL: ws://{MainboardIP}:3030/websocket. The same OpenCentauri docs list Alternative paths: /ws, /, /api/websocket, /sdcp.
- **Protocol:** The Smart Device Control Protocol (SDCP) v3.0.0 is an application layer protocol for interaction between clients and the Centauri Carbon FDM printer motherboard.
- **Connection limit:** One pycentauri source says the printer's SDCP server accepts up to 5 open WebSockets on port 3030; the 6th returns HTTP 500 with body "too many client". Any emulator should respect this.
- **Emulator:** The closest hit is a GitHub repo, resnbl/cc-emulator, which describes a desktop "emulator" that can record the status messages produced during a print by the real printer. It is a record-and-replay style tool rather than a full simulator. That result came from a mirror domain (github.xiaohuzi123231346.workers.dev), so verify it against the original repo before relying on it.
- **Reference implementations:** The pycentauri library (speaks the printer's native SDCP v3 protocol over its local WebSocket (port 3030)) and the OpenCentauri API documentation are the best starting points for building a simulator. Their message formats can be used as the spec.

I did not find a maintained, ready-made SDCP simulator for the CC1 in these results.

# GitHub issue 40: Elegoo Centauri Carbon cannot be connected from the printer chat

Written 2026-11-16. Nothing was changed in the repository, nothing was posted on GitHub, nothing was committed or pushed.

## What the person saw, reproduced

I used the released JusPrin 2.0.0 (/Applications/JusPrin.app) on a scratch copy of Kenneth's data folder. I added "Elegoo Centauri Carbon, 0.4 nozzle" through Home › + Add printer, then wrote "I want to connect it so I can send prints to it directly. Its IP is 192.168.1.77".

The model called the connect tool as Moonraker at 192.168.1.77:7125. The app refused it before sending any request: "This printer is saved with the Elegoo Link connection type, which this chat does not connect: it connects Moonraker and OctoPrint. You can still prepare prints and export a file." The model then offered a USB drive and offered to tell the developers. This matches the issue. It also explains why the issue footer says "Connection: Moonraker": the chat records the type the model asked for before the app refuses it. Screenshot: issue-40-shots/1-chat-refuses-elegoo-link.jpg.

## Where the limit comes from

- **OrcaSlicer upstream already supports the printer.** `src/slic3r/Utils/ElegooLink.cpp` (upstream commits 427d0f7a9f and 00a3e78f8a, both on upstream/main) tests a Centauri Carbon by fetching the printer's web page and looking for "ELEGOO". It uploads the file and starts the print over the printer's own protocol on port 3030. For a Centauri Carbon 2 it uses an access code instead. Every Elegoo profile ships with this connection type, including the Klipper-based Neptune 4 series.
- **The limit is JusPrin's own code.** `OrcaPrinterBackend::connection()` (OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:571-588) maps every type other than Moonraker and OctoPrint to "other" and marks the printer unavailable. `connect_host()` and the `printer_host_connect` schema in ToolRegistry.cpp accept only "moonraker" or "octoprint". This was a choice made on purpose: commit 67577ad993 (Sept 22) and commit 83a8431df2 (Nov 4). The Nov 4 commit names the Elegoo Neptune 4 case and changed only the message.
- **Sending already works for any connection type.** Once a printer has an address saved, JusPrin's Print button and the AI's print_dialog_open open OrcaSlicer's own send dialog (ShellController.cpp:1800-1835). They do not check the connection type.

## A workaround that works today

I checked this in the released app, against a local web page that answers the way upstream's test expects:

1. View › Switch to classic view…
2. Press the Wi-Fi icon beside "Printer". The "Physical Printer" dialog opens with Host Type already set to Elegoo Link.
3. Type the printer's IP address and press Test. It reported "Connection to ElegooLink is working correctly." Press OK.
4. Press "Back to JusPrin".

After this, the Home card read "Connected · Elegoo Link · <address>". Print opened "Send G-code to printer host" with an "Upload and Print" box. I did not press Upload: the stand-in page cannot take a file, and nobody here has a Centauri Carbon. So the upload itself is untested. It is upstream's code, and people in OrcaSlicer forums report that it works.

Screenshots: issue-40-shots/2, 3 and 4.

## OctoEverywhere

OctoEverywhere's help pages say a Centauri Carbon needs their "Elegoo Connect" plug-in, run on a Raspberry Pi or in Docker. I found no page saying that it gives a slicer an address to send prints to. That is unverified either way. The chat cannot set up a third-party service in any case.

## What it would take to connect from the chat (a proposal, not agreed)

- Accept "elegoolink" in `printer_host_connect` for printers saved with Elegoo Link.
- Add a connection test with the chat's 30-second limit, copied from upstream's Centauri test, the same way the Moonraker and OctoPrint tests were copied.
- Add an Elegoo Link section to the connect-print-host skill.
- Add unit tests in tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp, plus a check like the one above against a stand-in page.
- About a day of work, including the build.
- Two things stand in the way:
  - Kenneth's evidence rule for skill lines: a state must be seen for real. There is no Centauri Carbon here and no simulator exists.
  - The Centauri Carbon 2 asks for an access code, so the chat's key form needs new wording.

## A related problem in the same check (found, not fixed)

The refusal is decided by the type the printer was *saved* with, and a printer just added from the catalogue is saved with its profile's default type. That default is never something the person chose. Base profiles from 12 vendors set a type the chat refuses: Creality 33 (the K1 and K2 family), SeeMeCNC 28, Elegoo 18, Prusa 14, and smaller vendors. So a Neptune 4 or a Creality K1, both of which run Moonraker, cannot be connected as Moonraker from the chat either. One possible fix (a proposal): refuse only when an address is already saved with another type.

## Side observation, one chat

Right after the printer was added, the model wrote: "The result from adding the printer also contained a block of instructions about connecting through Moonraker or OctoPrint. It isn't part of what you asked for, so I'm ignoring it." That block is the app's own connection skill. If this repeats, the model may be discarding the skill. One chat is not enough to call it a rate.

input.recap: Issue 40 is reproduced in the released JusPrin 2.0.0, and a workaround through OrcaSlicer's classic view works up to the send dialog. Nothing in the repository changed and nothing was posted, committed or pushed. Whether the chat should support Elegoo Link is Kenneth's call.

content.text:
I reproduced issue 40 in the released JusPrin 2.0.0. The chat refuses printers saved as Elegoo Link by design, but there is a workaround that works today. Adding Elegoo Link to the chat is a decision for Kenneth, so I wrote up a finding and built nothing. Nothing in the repository changed, and nothing was posted, committed or pushed. The full finding and four screenshots are in the shared notes folder as `issue-40-elegoo-link-finding.md` and `issue-40-shots/`.

**What the reporter saw.** I added an Elegoo Centauri Carbon and asked the chat to connect it at an IP address. The model tried a Moonraker connection, and the app refused before sending any request: "This printer is saved with the Elegoo Link connection type, which this chat does not connect." The model then offered a USB drive. The chat records the type the model asked for before the refusal, which is why the issue's footer says "Connection: Moonraker".

**Where the limit is.**
- **Upstream supports the printer.** OrcaSlicer's `ElegooLink.cpp` can test a Centauri Carbon, upload a file and start a print.
- **JusPrin's chat blocks it.** The chat's connect code accepts only Moonraker and OctoPrint and calls everything else unavailable (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:571-588`, and the `printer_host_connect` tool's schema). The commits from Sept 22 and Nov 4 made that choice on purpose.
- **Sending already works for any connection type.** Once a printer has an address saved, Print opens OrcaSlicer's own send dialog.

**Workaround.** I checked this in the released app against a local web page that answers like the printer's:
1. View › Switch to classic view…
2. Press the Wi-Fi icon beside Printer. Host Type is already Elegoo Link.
3. Type the IP and press Test. It said "Connection to ElegooLink is working correctly."
4. Press OK, then Back to JusPrin.

Afterwards the Home card read "Connected · Elegoo Link", and Print opened "Send G-code to printer host" with "Upload and Print". The upload itself is untested, because nobody here has a Centauri Carbon.

**OctoEverywhere.** Its help pages say this printer needs their "Elegoo Connect" plug-in. I found nothing saying it gives a slicer an address to send prints to, so that is unverified either way.

**What chat support would take (a proposal).** Accept Elegoo Link in the connect tool, copy upstream's Centauri test with the chat's 30-second limit, add an Elegoo Link section to the connection skill, and add tests. That is about a day of work. Two things block it now:
- Kenneth's rule is that skill lines describe states seen on a real printer. There is no Centauri Carbon here and I found no simulator.
- The Centauri Carbon 2 asks for an access code, so the chat's key form needs new wording.

**Related problem, not fixed.** The chat decides by the type a printer was saved with, and a newly added printer gets its profile's default, which the person never chose. Base profiles from 12 vendors use a default the chat refuses, including Creality's K1 and K2 family, all Elegoo printers and Prusa. So a Neptune 4 or a Creality K1, which both run Moonraker, can't be connected as Moonraker from the chat either.

**One-chat observation.** Right after adding the printer, the model said the app's connection skill text looked like a "block of instructions" and that it would ignore it. One chat isn't enough to call it a pattern.

Sources: [OpenCentauri API docs](https://suchmememanyskill.github.io/OpenCentauri/software/api), [pycentauri](https://pypi.org/project/pycentauri/), [OctoEverywhere Elegoo help](https://help.octoeverywhere.com/help-docs/printers/elegoo/elegoo-connect-vs-klipper.md), [SimplyPrint: Centauri Carbon and OctoPrint](https://simplyprint.io/uk/compatibility/elegoo-centauri-carbon/octoprint-setup), [BambuStudio PR 9489](https://github.com/bambulab/BambuStudio/pull/9489).
Ignore OctoEverywhere. Check the Git log or the historical sessions to see if there's any rationale behind allowing only Octoprint and Moonraker

### 1. Bambu printers are saved before they're connected, so data the printer reports goes unused

**Problem.** A Bambu printer on the network broadcasts its model before any login, but reports its nozzle diameter and loaded filament (AMS slots, external spool) only after it's connected. The branch saves the printer first and asks the user for the nozzle. Then, at connect time, `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer` compares the saved nozzle with the reported one and refuses to connect if they differ. The data that could have filled the answer in is only used to reject a wrong answer.

**Solution.** For a Bambu printer found on the network or in the signed-in account, connect first:
- Tapping the printer asks for its access code in a page-owned field, or offers sign-in.
- Wait for the printer's first status report.
- Fill the pinned card's nozzle and spools, marked as reported by the printer.
- Ask only for the build plate, which no printer reports.
- One tap saves a printer that is already connected.

I added this as a section to `issue-40-elegoo-link-finding.md` in the shared notes folder.
What's your suggestion?

My suggestion: let the printer chat connect every connection type that OrcaSlicer itself supports, by running OrcaSlicer's own connection test for each type. Separately, reply on issue 40 now with the workaround. Nothing on record says other types were meant to be refused, Kenneth asked for "others" twice, and upstream already has a working test for each type. This is a proposal; nothing has been agreed or built.

**What would change.**
- **Use the type the printer is saved with.** When the person asks to connect a printer saved as Elegoo Link, Creality Print, PrusaLink, Duet and so on, the chat runs that type's test from OrcaSlicer, the same one the classic view's Test button runs. I checked that button against an Elegoo stand-in page today. If the test passes, the address is saved, and Print already sends through OrcaSlicer's send dialog. No per-type code is copied, except the existing Moonraker and OctoPrint tests, which stay as they are.
- **Let a newly added printer connect as Moonraker.** A printer that has no address saved yet carries only its profile's default type, which the person never chose. Such a printer may also connect as Moonraker or OctoPrint. That fixes the Neptune 4 and the Creality K1, which run Moonraker and are refused today.
- **Add one short paragraph to the connection skill.** For other types, the app runs OrcaSlicer's own test, and the result is OrcaSlicer's message. It would make no claims about a type that nobody has seen work.

**Known gaps.**
- Upstream's tests have no upper time limit. A printer that accepts the connection and never answers would keep the chat waiting until the network gives up.
- A Centauri Carbon 2 asks for an access code, and the existing key form says "API key". That is the same label OrcaSlicer's dialog uses ("API Key / Password").

- The real app against an Elegoo stand-in page, as I did today.

75:A fixed, mechanical step of a workflow can be a tool. Examples are generating OrcaSlicer's calibration geometry and starting OrcaSlicer's slice action. Advice should stay a skill until there is a separately specified operation behind it that always behaves the same way.
77:## Skills versus tools
79:A skill is text the model reads. A tool is something the app executes. To decide which one a candidate is, ask one question: does it have to run, or does it only have to be read?
82:- It only has to be read if it is judgement, the order to do things in, facts about printing, how to interpret a tool's result, or which question to ask first. That makes it a skill.
84:The section above covers tools. This section covers skills, and decides the cases that fall in between.
86:A skill contains things the model could do by itself if it had the right knowledge. It contains nothing that executes. Examples:
93:A skill is a file on the Agent page, `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: frontmatter with its `name` and a `trigger`, a `description` or both, then the text the model gets. The page sends every skill once per connection with the `skills` bridge message. A skill with a trigger is the app's: when the event it names happens, the host adds it to the one request where the model first reads about the event, as the request's last item, and to no later request. A skill with a description is the model's: `skill_read` lists the described skills in its own description and returns one by name, and is offered only while at least one exists. One skill has a description and a trigger: `calibration`, read when a print problem may come from the filament or its settings, when the person asks to calibrate, or in a calibration project, and fired by `calibration_started` on the first turn of a calibration project's chat; it carries the conversation of a calibration (when a test is worth it, the two facts said before the person's project closes, asking which test only when the handover leaves it open, per-test ranges and how to read the print, the naming rule for the saved preset), while `calibration_generate`'s description keeps only that tool's rules. Four other skills have triggers, one file each:
96:- `project-setup-changed` (trigger `setup_changed`): check the setup in force against the print's purpose. It fires on the result of an in-app `setup_record` that recorded a purpose for the first time or changed it (its result says which in `purposeChange`; a call that restates the same purpose, or leaves it out, to change the plan does not fire it), when the printer, filament, process or plate type differs from the setup the model was last asked to check under a recorded purpose (on the next tool result of the turn, or on the next turn's first request when the person changed it by hand), on a turn's first request after the person restored an earlier version while a purpose is recorded, and on every turn's first request while the plan is marked `needs_reassessment` (2026-10-28: the model may leave recording the plan to the turn that answers its question about the change, and that turn finds the setup checked already, so without this the mark could outlive every skill that explains it). Each time the model is asked to check, the app saves the setup in force as the one checked. The model's own successful `printer_setup` fires nothing: the setup it chose is saved as checked at once (Kenneth, 2026-10-19), so the skill is for a setup that moved without the model, and a pairing its change breaks is caught by the slice-refusal facts and skill. It gives way to the file-loaded skill on a request that carries both, since that skill already asks for the same check.
97:- `slice-failed` (trigger `slice_failed`): a plate's last slice did not succeed, because OrcaSlicer's check refused the plate or the run failed. The adapter records why on the plate (`WorkspacePlate::slice_failure`: refused or failed, OrcaSlicer's words, the setting and object when named) at the moment it happens (a hook in `Plater::reslice`, `Workspace/SliceRequests.hpp`, and the run's completion event), worded by the print-issue monitor's `slice_failure_of`, and keeps it until the plate slices. Every request carries it as the plate's `sliceFailure`; `slice_report` of an unsliced plate adds the check code and the object's name. The skill fires once per failure, on the first request that carries it: the result of the model's own `slice_start`, the turn the app starts when a slice the model started fails after its turn, or the next message after the person's Slice all. The same refusal again is the same failure.
98:- `print-issues` (trigger `print_issues`): what the print-issue chip's Ask AI button asks for and how to read what OrcaSlicer reports. The adapter reads a slice's warnings through the monitor's `slice_warnings_of` while the plate is active and keeps a summary on the plate while that slice is current (`WorkspacePlate::slice_warnings`: the count, how many the person ignored, and the first warning, critical first, in OrcaSlicer's words with its setting and object). It counts every warning the chip lists. The chip and `slice_report` read the same slice-result rule (`Workspace/SliceResultWarnings`), so they list the same warnings, except that `slice_report` also lists the timelapse ones, marked `appliesWhen: "timelapse"`, which the chip does not count. Every request carries it as the plate's `sliceWarnings`. The skill fires on the request that carries a chip's message, and on the first request whose workspace shows warnings no request has carried yet, whether the person sliced (their next message) or the model did (the tool result that shows them, or the app's turn when its slice ended after its turn); a re-slice with the same warnings fires nothing.
102:- **A procedure made of existing tool calls.** It is a skill for as long as carrying it out takes judgement. It becomes a tool only when the steps are fixed and the person wants the whole thing as one action that can be undone. If there are many such fixed sequences, they go in one workflow registry (see [When resources or skills are appropriate](#when-resources-or-skills-are-appropriate)).
103:- **An analysis.** It is a tool when OrcaSlicer computes it and always gets the same answer, such as overhang angles from geometry. It is a skill when it is a judgement about evidence. Pair that skill with the tool that supplies the evidence (`view_render`, `slice_report`).
105:- **A tool description versus a skill.** A tool description says when to call that one tool, in the words a person would use. A skill says how several tools fit together and what to conclude from their results. If a tool description has grown into a step-by-step procedure, move the procedure out into a skill.
107:When you are not sure, start with a skill. A skill is a text file that ships with the page. A tool costs the whole implementation sequence described below, including fakes, tests, and rebase evidence. Turn a skill into a tool only on the kind of evidence every tool starts from (see [Start with an eval failure](#start-with-an-eval-failure)). Either transcripts show the model getting the sequence wrong in ways that better text does not fix, or the action needs something only the app can give: all-or-nothing application, validation, or undo. The opposite sign exists too. If a skill has turned into exact values and calls in a fixed order, with no judgement between them, it should be written as a tool.
109:How something gets loaded into the model's context does not decide whether it is a skill or a tool. Today a skill costs its one line in the instructions, and a tool costs its definition on the first request of a conversation (see [Tool budget and tool shape](#tool-budget-and-tool-shape)). If we later use the model platform's deferred loading, both will cost one index line plus a load when needed. A skill could then be a deferred read-only tool: the tool's description is the skill's index line, and the tool's result is the skill's text. Tools and skills would then be found the same way and covered by the same eval.
176:One tool is added during a conversation, on purpose. `issue_report_open` comes with the Bambu connection skill (`PrinterConversation::connection_skill`, carried as `AgentSkillUse::tools`). It is offered from the request where the skill is first sent, including the continuation after the tool result that brought the skill, and on every request after that. The skill, and so the tool, comes into force once the chat has a saved Bambu Lab printer: with `printer_add`'s result, or on the first request of a chat about one. A chat with no saved Bambu Lab printer never has it. Adding it costs that chat one prompt-cache miss, and that cost was accepted. The list stays the same from then on. This is not deferral: no tool search, no `defer_loading`, and no toolsets. The app decides when the tool is offered, and the model never asks for it.
279:`ToolDefinition` currently stores the name, title, description, input and output schemas, action class, exposure, availability, and handler. The other properties are not registry fields. # Writing a connection skill

Draft of 2026-11-04 for Kenneth's review. Nothing here is agreed yet. Where a sentence describes code or a test, it describes what is on `jusprin-newui` at e27c962864; where it proposes a rule, it says so.

A connection skill is the text the app adds to a printer chat when a person tries to connect a printer of one connection type: `AgentUI/src/skills/connect-bambu/SKILL.md`, `connect-moonraker` and `connect-octoprint`. Read this before writing a new one or changing one. The general rules for skills, and for when a skill becomes a tool, are in [Tool extension guide, Skills versus tools](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md#skills-versus-tools); this document adds only what connecting a printer needs.

## What the skill is for

Kenneth's test, 2026-11-02: the skill is good if the agent guides a person who is stuck and makes educated guesses it labels as guesses, until the printer is connected or the person chooses to leave it. It is not judged by whether a printer connected, by how many states it names, or by whether every sentence in it is true. A skill that is never wrong and never helps a stuck person fails the test.

Three times in three days a skill was written to the wrong half of that test. The first Bambu skill was a table from state to next step, and on the real P1S it told a person with the right access code to re-check it. The second Bambu skill said "add no cause of your own", and the model repeated a false reason instead of guessing. The host skills said "you have not seen where Mainsail or Fluidd show the key", and on 2026-11-04 the model told a person who had no key to look in "Mainsail's settings page", which does not show it. Each time the writer kept "say nothing false" and dropped "help the stuck person".

## How the skill reaches the model

Facts about the code today.

- The app chooses the skill from the connection type and adds it to the conversation once, with the result of the first `printer_connection_status` or `printer_connect` call, or on the first request of a chat opened to connect (`PrinterConversation::connection_skill`, `AgentHost::session_skill`). The model never picks it. For a print host the type is known only from the first `printer_connect`'s `hostType` or a saved connection, so a host skill never arrives before the model has asked for an address and called connect.
- The skill stays in the chat once sent (`AgentSkillUse::stays`).
- Everything before that call runs on the standing prompt alone (`AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`): the offer to connect after adding, the request for an address, the first connect call. A skill cannot guide those turns.
- The skill opens with "The rules above still apply", so wherever the standing prompt gives an exact sentence or an exact step, the prompt wins over a fact in the skill. On 2026-11-04 the prompt's finishing example "It is connected, so you can send prints straight to it" beat the skill's "verified means Moonraker answered, and nothing more", with Klipper shut down.

## Before writing: three audits

### 1. The person's stuck moments, not the app's states

Start from the moments a person with this connection type gets stuck, and write to those. The failure table (which error text means which step) comes second. The three moments every connection type has:

- **Giving the address.** What do they open in a browser, which port, what if the name does not resolve. For a host, this moment happens before the skill arrives, so what the person needs here belongs in the standing prompt or the skill's trigger has to move.
- **Being asked for a credential they do not have.** A Klipper owner who has never heard of an API key; a Bambu owner who cannot find the access code. The skill says, in order of cost to check, what is likeliest and what they can look at, each labelled as observed, documented or a guess. The 401-without-a-key case was the one place both 2026-11-04 runs got stuck, and the skill had only "search for where their version shows it".
- **Being told it is connected.** What "verified" proved and did not prove, so the closing sentence does not promise what the app has not checked.

For each moment, write what a competent friend would say to someone standing at that screen. That sentence is the skill's job; the error table supports it.

### 2. Information against knowledge, per state

Kenneth, 2026-11-02: for each failure, is the cause a lack or wrong *information* (a fact about this situation that only the app can know at that moment) or a lack or wrong *knowledge* (how things work)? Information belongs in the app's note or tool result; knowledge about connecting belongs in the skill; how to work in general belongs in the prompt.

Before writing a line of the skill, list the app's notes for this connection type and, for each, what the app knows at that moment that the model would need. Where the note lacks it, the fix is to the note, and the skill is written against the note that will exist. Examples found on 2026-11-04 for Moonraker:

- The failure note after HTTP 401 does not say whether the form was submitted empty or with a key, although `PrinterConversation::connect` holds the credential string. The model told a person who typed nothing that "it rejected the key".
- The verified note carries no Klipper state, although `Moonraker::test` reads `klippy_state` from `/server/info` and only logs it. The model said "you can send prints straight to it" to a printer whose Klipper was shut down.

The Bambu note was enriched after the 2026-11-02 incident (the plug-in's code, how long it took, a TCP look at port 8883 before and after). That fix was made once and never made a rule; this audit is the rule. Proposed.

### 3. The standing prompt and the tool descriptions

List every sentence in `printerInstructions.ts` and in the connection tools' descriptions (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`) that gives an exact wording, an exact step or a procedure for connecting. Each one either goes, becomes conditional, or is accepted knowing the skill cannot override it. On 2026-11-04 three such sentences caused failures the skill's facts should have prevented: the "offer it once … with exactly" sentence after `printer_add` (asked a person who had already asked to connect), "say briefly to use that form" after `credential_requested` (told a person with no key to type one), and the finishing example above. The connect tool's "until they give one, ask for it instead of calling this" made the model ask permission to try a port the person had just said to try.

This matches [Tool extension guide, A tool description versus a skill](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md#skills-versus-tools): a description that has grown into a step belongs in the skill. The skill work added new text and never swept the old. Proposed as a required step.

## Writing the skill

### Explain the mechanism as a chain

Number the steps the connection goes through, each depending on the one before, and say so: a step that worked says nothing about the ones after it. This is what let Sonnet 5.5 reason about failures the skill did not list on 2026-11-03 (an OctoPrint the person called Klipper; `https://` against a plain-http host). Keep the chain from the person's side as well as the app's: for Moonraker, the app reaches Moonraker at its port, and so does the person's browser, so Moonraker's own pages, the key page included, are at that same address and port. The 2026-11-04 skill explained only the app's side, and the model sent the person to a port-80 URL for the key.

### Three kinds of statement, each labelled

- **Observed on a real host or printer.** What the app's own test reported, and when (the guard tests in `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` require every state the skill names to have a dated run behind it). Write these as facts.
- **Documented.** What a maintainer's docs or FAQ say, named ("Moonraker's docs say…", "Mainsail's FAQ for this error says…"). Write these with their source. The evidence rule does not forbid them; leaving them out is what made the host skills silent about the one thing a stuck Klipper owner needs (that a 401 from a printer on the same home network is usually fixed in `trusted_clients`, with no key at all).
- **A guess.** General knowledge nobody has checked on this setup. Write it as a guess and give the cheapest check.

What not to write, each from an incident:

- One next step per state. The state-to-step table sent a person with the right code to re-check it (P1S, 2026-11-02).
- "Add no cause of your own" or anything that forbids reasoning. The model repeated a false reason (P1S, 2026-11-02). The guard bans the phrase.
- A menu path as fact (`Settings > WLAN`). The guard bans arrows and "Settings >".
- A menu path as a presupposition. "Search for where Mainsail shows the key" presupposes it does; the model filled it in with "Mainsail's settings page" (2026-11-04). Say what is known instead: Mainsail and Fluidd do not show it; the two ways to get it; when it is not needed.
- A sentence the standing prompt contradicts with an exact wording. The prompt wins; see audit 3.
- A fix as the single answer. "Restart the printer" became every chat's advice once it was the only untested suggestion listed (P1S, 2026-11-02).

### Search: say what to look up and how to read it

Every chat has the provider's web search. Two things are known about it. Offered with no instruction, the model did not search once in four chats (2026-11-02). Told to search before guessing, it searched in two of seven chats and cited its source (2026-11-03). Told to search for the key, it found Moonraker's docs, which give the key page without a port, and handed the person a wrong URL (2026-11-04).

So the skill names the search for each stuck moment and says how to apply the result to this setup: what the docs assume (Moonraker's default port), what varies by version, and what the model should ask the person to confirm. "Search before you say" alone was not enough.

### The length

The skill is read on every request after it arrives. The three skills today are 50 to 60 lines. A stuck-moment section for the credential adds a paragraph, not a page.

## The app's part

The skill is only as good as the notes it reads. For each connection type, the notes carry what audit 2 found (proposed; the Bambu note does this today, the host notes do not):

- A failed connection: the host's own words, forwarded unchanged ([How to fix a result that hides the failure](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md#how-to-fix-a-result-that-hides-the-failure)), plus what the app itself did and saw: whether a credential was sent, how long the test waited, what a port answered.
- A verified connection: what the app checked and anything it read on the way that bears on the next step, such as Klipper's state.
- The report card: today it is shown at exactly the second failure in a chat (`PrinterConversation::connection_failed`). A 401 after a wrong-port failure counted as the second failure on 2026-11-04 although it was progress. Whether the rule should count repeats of the same outcome instead is open.

## Testing a connection skill

### Offline, today

- `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp`: the skill arrives only once the type is known and never in a chat that only adds a printer; every state named in backquotes has a dated real run; banned phrases are absent.
- `AgentUI/src/skills.test.ts` and `wording.test.ts`: the file parses, the trigger is unique, the text says "the app" and never "arrives".
- The shell harness's `--print-host-check` (hosts) and `--printer-connect-skill` (the P1S): the app's own connection test against a real host or printer with no model, the source of every "observed" line.

These prove where the skill arrives and that its facts were seen. They say nothing about whether its words help.

### Live, with Kenneth's test

The 2026-11-03 host chats ran Sonnet 5.5 against Docker hosts with a scripted person who had the key, took the port advice, and knew it was OctoPrint. All seven connected and nothing was learned about guidance. The 2026-11-04 chats ran GPT-5.4 Mini with a person who did not know what an API key was, and failed at every stuck moment.

So a live run of a connection skill (proposed):

- scripts a person who does **not** have the answer at each stuck moment: no key and no idea what one is; the Mainsail port; a `.local` name; Klipper shut down; the wrong host type;
- runs on the weakest model the product offers by default, not only on the model the writer prefers;
- is judged by where the person ends up (`ended_badly` in `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`), including the closing sentence, not by whether the printer connected;
- reads the transcript as the model saw it, every tool call, result and note in order, before any line of the skill is changed, and names for each failure the text the model saw or lacked.

Live runs cost money and need Kenneth's approval of a specific batch with a token estimate.

## Checklist before a connection skill is committed

1. The three stuck moments are written to, each with labelled guesses in order of cost.
2. Audit 2 is written down: for each note, what the app knows and what the note says; the gaps are fixed or listed.
3. Audit 3 is written down: every exact connecting sentence in the prompt and the tool descriptions, and what was done with it.
4. Every state in backquotes has a dated real run; the guard passes.
5. Every documented claim names its source; every guess says it is one; no menu is stated or presupposed.
6. Each search the skill asks for says what to search and how to apply the answer.
7. A stuck-person live run on the default model, approved and run, with the transcript read before any edit.

## Where the rules come from

- 2026-10-31, P1S: the app hid a cloud-mode printer and the model invented menus. Tools report what the app saw.
- 2026-11-01: "a general process that improves when more people are using it" (Kenneth); tool results carry what is true now, a skill carries how it works.
- 2026-11-02: the state-to-step table failed on the real P1S; "guide the user… make educated guess"; "the goal here is not to connect my printer"; information against knowledge, and where each belongs.
- 2026-11-02 to 03: web search alone was never used; told to search, the model did, in some chats.
- 2026-11-03: the host skills were written from Docker evidence and proven with a person who knew the answers; "apply the lessons" was done from memory, and search was left out of them by mistake.
- 2026-11-04: two live Moonraker runs on GPT-5.4 Mini failed at each stuck moment. Diagnosis and lessons review in the side-session notes of 2026-11-04 (`moonraker-skill-diagnosis.md`, `connection-skill-lessons-review.md`).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **JusPrin** is a fork of OrcaSlicer. Fork code lives in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Attribute behaviour by `git blame` plus `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`.
   - **The printer chat** (`PrinterConversation`) connects host printers with the `printer_host_connect` tool. Today it accepts only `hostType` "moonraker" or "octoprint".
   - `OrcaPrinterBackend::connection()` maps every other `PrintHostType` to "other" and returns state "unavailable" with the message "This printer is saved with the X connection type, which this chat does not connect...".
   - **Upstream's print-host classes** come from `PrintHost::get_print_host(config)`, with `test(wxString&)`. `format_error` gives "HTTP %u: body" when the host answered with a status.
   - **Upstream `ElegooLink`** classifies by printer_model:
     - Centauri Carbon (CC): GET "/" and look for "ELEGOO".
     - Centauri Carbon 2 (CC2): `system/info` with an X-Token, default "123456"; 401 or 403 means "Invalid access code".
     - Others: OctoPrint's test.
     - Upload: chunked upload to `uploadFile/upload`, then starts the print over a websocket on port 3030.
   - **Upstream Http** defaults: `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_CONNECT` 10 s, `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MAX` 0 (no limit). JusPrin's copied tests set `timeout_max(kConnectionWait)` (30 s).
   - **Cloud hosts** (`is_cloud`): Obico, SimplyPrint, 3DPrinterOS need a sign-in, so exclude them from the chat. PrusaConnect is a subclass of PrusaLink.
   - **PrusaLink sign-in:** `printhost_authorization_type` is atKeyPassword (X-Api-Key) or atUserPassword (digest, `printhost_user`/`printhost_password`).
   - **Window calls:** `ShowModal` in OctoPrint and ElegooLink appears only in upload, so the tests are safe to run on a worker thread.
   - **Sending is already type-agnostic:** `ShellController::open_print_dialog` opens the print_host dialog whenever `print_host` is set.
   - **Profile defaults:** base profiles in 12 vendors set a type the chat refuses — Creality 33, SeeMeCNC 28, Elegoo 18, Prusa 14, iQ 8, Volumic 6, Flashforge 5, and others. The Neptune 4 and Creality K1 run Moonraker but are refused.

# Connecting a printer through a print host

The rules above still apply. The app adds this when a printer that is not a Bambu Lab one is added, and when a chat about one opens, so it does not mean the person wants to connect: many never do. Start connecting only once they say they want to. Right after a printer is added, unless they have already said whether they want it connected, offer it once: end that reply with exactly "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" and then "Choices: Connect it | Not now". When they have already asked to connect it, go straight on.

Once they want to connect, your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention. Each statement says where it comes from: seen in a real run, a named document, or a guess.

## Which connection type

printer_host_connect needs to know which program the app talks to, its `hostType`. printer_connection_status gives the type this printer is saved with. Until a connection is saved, that type is only the default in the printer's profile, which the person never chose: an Elegoo printer's profile names Elegoo Link, and a Prusa's names PrusaLink (from the app's printer profiles). Use it unless what the person says shows their printer runs something else.

- **A Klipper printer is reached through Moonraker** (`moonraker`), the program beside Klipper that other apps talk to over the network. People usually use it through a web page in a browser, Mainsail or Fluidd. The app talks only to Moonraker. A printer whose page is Mainsail or Fluidd runs Moonraker, whatever its profile says.
- **OctoPrint runs on a computer beside the printer and drives it** (`octoprint`). People use it through OctoPrint's own web page. The app talks only to OctoPrint, never to the printer itself.
- **Elegoo Link** (`elegoolink`): see below.
- **Every other type** printer_host_connect lists runs the app's own test for that type, the one the app's printer connection window runs, and has not been tried here against a real printer. Its failures come in that test's words, which may be in the app's language. The app sends an address and one key. From the app's code, these need more, and cannot be finished from this chat: Repetier, which also needs the printer chosen on the host; UltiMaker, which needs a user name and password; and PrusaLink set up with a user name and password instead of a key. The person can finish those in the app's own window for it: View › Switch to classic view…, then the Wi-Fi icon beside "Printer" (seen 2026-11-16).

When the person does not know whether they have Moonraker or OctoPrint, ask what the page they open to control the printer is called, or what it shows. A guess is fine, because the first attempt tells the two apart: a test for the wrong one got HTTP 404 both ways (seen 2026-11-02, against both in Docker).

## Elegoo Link

From the app's code for Elegoo Link (read 2026-11-16). It tells Elegoo printers apart by the model the person picked in the app, not by asking the printer:

- **Centauri Carbon.** The test asks for the printer's own web page at the address, and passes when that page contains "ELEGOO". It uses no key. "ElegooLink not detected" means something answered there, but not with that page. The address is the printer's IP address, with no port.
- **Centauri Carbon 2.** The test asks the printer for its information with an access code, and with none it sends 123456. A refused code got HTTP 401 or 403, and then the app's form asks for it. The form says "API key": for this printer, say it is the printer's access code. Where the printer shows its code is not in the app's code, so search before you say.
- **Any other Elegoo printer, such as a Neptune 4.** The app runs OctoPrint's test. That the Neptune 4 runs Klipper with Moonraker is general knowledge, not tried here: when the Elegoo Link test fails on one, Moonraker at port 7125 is the likeliest next try.

## The address

Ask for the address they open that page at, including any port.

- **Moonraker:** the app needs Moonraker's own address, port 7125 unless it was changed, as in `http://192.168.1.50:7125`. The address of the Mainsail page answered too where that page passed the app's requests on to Moonraker, as a usual Mainsail setup does. A Mainsail page that did not pass them on answered with a web page instead (both seen 2026-11-02 in Docker). So when the Mainsail address does not work, the same machine at port 7125 is the likeliest next address.
- **OctoPrint:** the address they open OctoPrint at.
- The address can be an IP address or a name, but a name this computer cannot look up got no answer at all (seen 2026-11-02 with a `.local` name no device answered to).
- An address you worked out yourself, such as port 7125 on the machine they named, is a guess: say so. When they say to try it, call printer_host_connect with it at once, without asking again.

Used 2026-10-12 for the spiral vase investigation (branch `claude/spiral-vase-writable`).

**Recipe.** Start `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --manual-mcp <scratch dir>` with `HOME=<scratch home>`, wait for `HARNESS MCP FIXTURE READY` on stderr (about 15 s), read the URL from `<scratch dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`, then call tools with `probe.call(urlsplit(url), "tools/call", {"name": ..., "arguments": ...})` imported from `tests/mcp/probe.py`. The fixture is two plates, one 20 mm box each, Bambu X1C 0.4, "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C", "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C", the same presets as Kenneth's live tests. Another session's harness can run at the same time; the port falls back from 47301 and the discovery file is per data dir.

**Trap 1: leaked harness.** In a script, `cd "$S" && nohup harness ... &` makes `$!` the subshell, so `kill $!` leaves the harness running, and the next run's `rm -rf <fixture>` fails with "Directory not empty". Write `cd "$S"; nohup harness ... &`. Check with `pgrep -fl "<worktree>.*JusPrinShellHarness"` before finishing.

**Trap 2: slice_start on a sliced, unchanged plate.** The fixture's plate 1 starts sliced. `slice_start` on it (with or without `wait`) left it reported `sliced: false`, `slice_report` `valid: false`, and with `wait: true` the probe saw the stream close with no reply. Orca's log says "background process in idle state, use previous result". Change a setting first, then slice. Not investigated further.

**Timings on this Mac, Release config, load 30 to 40:** fresh worktree build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests workspace_contract_tests setting_display_tests shell_integration_harness` was 905 steps in about 14 min; the shell harness default regression (549 checks) about 2 min; the workspace adapter harness (972 checks) under 1 min. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

**Seeding a preset (2026-10-12).** `--manual-mcp` does not wipe its directory at start, so a user preset written to `<fixture>/user/default/machine/<name>.json` before launch (keys `from: User`, `inherits`, `name`, `printer_settings_id`, `version`, plus the values under test) is loaded and can be named as a settings `target.preset`. A Python driver that starts the harness with `subprocess.Popen` and terminates it in `finally` avoids Trap 1.


**Why a plate will not slice (2026-10-15).** MCP `slice_report` on a plate Orca refuses says only `valid: false`, with no reason even with `sections: ["findings"]`, and `slice_start` still answers `started: true`. Orca's own refusal text is in `<fixture>/log/debug_*.log`: grep `validate err=`. Used to reproduce the PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate case (branch `claude/bed-type-mismatch`, worktree distracted-lehmann-9c1b12). See [[printer-setup-bed-type-check]].

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.

- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

description: "Traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control: in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args and @import failures, the model picker needs page JS, a debugger attach once hung a slice."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-12T18:04:04.144Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.
